title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.0.1-rc.4
summary: Queued multi-file drag/drop, one progress window, maximum transfer speed, and receiver-confirmed completion. Update BOTH PCs to RC4 before testing: file batches use a new versioned protocol over the existing encrypted clipboard connection. Real-PC testing is still required.
changes: Drag several files together, or add another drag during a copy: each drag keeps an immutable source list and joins the transfer queue. The receiver waits instead of rejecting another transfer after three seconds.
Use one transfer window per PC with file/status rows, current-file progress, and Cancel all. Successful queues close automatically after cleanup; errors remain visible.

Remove speed selections and deliberate rate limiting. Progress painting avoids repeated tooltip updates and layout changes. New transfers restore and bring the window forward without stealing focus on progress ticks.
Acknowledge each new-protocol file only after the receiver saves it; retain completed files when a later file fails, keep duplicate names, and clean up incomplete files.
Show the drag cursor as soon as the drag announcement arrives, ignore stale show messages after drop/cancel, and stop unrelated clipboard connections from clearing an in-progress drag.
Include all RC3 hardening and add encrypted multi-file, queue-order, cancellation, malformed-manifest, and overlapping-connection regression coverage.
testing: Exit MWB on BOTH PCs. Back up your EXE/preferences, replace only the EXE, and confirm About says 1.0.1-rc.4 on each.
Drag three disposable files together, including an empty file and a large file. Confirm every file appears in one window on each PC and arrives intact.
While a large copy runs, drag two more files. Both windows should show them queued; they should copy without the RC3 disconnect error.
Type in a text editor during a transfer. Check that the cursor stays hidden while typing and that progress does not steal focus. Full-speed transfers may still cause mouse lag.
Minimize the transfer window, then add another drag. It should restore. Once all files finish successfully, both windows should close automatically.
Cancel from each PC in separate attempts, including while files are queued. Confirm no incomplete destination files appear and a new transfer works afterward.
Send a duplicate filename; confirm both files survive. Disconnect Wi-Fi during a large copy, reconnect, and drag again; errors should stay visible.
Check the drag icon when crossing screens slowly and quickly. Recheck single-file clipboard copy/paste, Unicode text, screenshots, reconnect, lock/unlock, and sleep/wake.
known_limitations: Use RC4 on both PCs. New queued drag/drop batches are not compatible with older MWB file-transfer implementations. Mouse/keyboard packets and underlying AES encryption are unchanged.
No folders, pause/resume, automatic retry, content-hash receipt, or direct Explorer-window targeting yet. Dragged files still save under Desktop\MouseWithoutBorders.
A drag may contain up to 256 files. Cancel all stops active and waiting items; a file already being committed may finish. Earlier completed files remain.
Maximum speed may increase Wi-Fi mouse lag. Hardware validation of focus, cursor hiding, drag feedback, and two-PC transfer behavior remains necessary.
Legacy clipboard copy/paste still uses the existing single-file transport and receive guard. Receiver-confirmed completion and multi-file queues apply to the new drag/drop path.
Hard termination or power loss may leave a .partial file. No Windows service or protected UAC/sign-in support is included.
